items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: would I come up and start a jazz piano course when he became President, and I said I'd be glad to. And I did.

ctx.x: Yeah, all in the show. Americana.

And the top ballet dancers, Dolan and Markova, of that day -- and the director was a top man, Moss Hart. And the show, called Seven Lively Arts, played at the Ziegfeld Theatre, which Billy Rose owned -- he bought that theatre. And that lasted for quite awhile, and then I met William Shuman during rehearsals there, and we had a lot of serious talks, and he told me, he was gonna be the new President of Juilliard, and would I come up and start a jazz piano course when he became President, and I said I'd be glad to.…
the show, I started in about 1945, I guess, and lasted for about 8 years -- and I taught the jazz piano in summer school.
